views.name: svc_requests_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  created_date AS created_ts,
  closed_date AS closed_ts,
  resolution_action_updated_date AS resolution_updated_ts,
  status,
  status_notes,
  agency_name,
  category,
  complaint_type,
  descriptor,
  incident_address,
  supervisor_district,
  neighborhood,
  location,
  source,
  media_url,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  police_district,
  -- derived convenience columns
  CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM created_date) AS DATE) AS created_date_only,
  CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM closed_date) AS DATE) AS closed_date_only,
  -- request duration in seconds when both timestamps present
  SAFE_CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(closed_date, created_date, SECOND) AS INT64) AS duration_seconds
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_311.311_service_requests`
views.description: Cleaned/normalized view of 311 service requests: casts and canonicalizes key columns, extracts dates, and exposes location coordinates and text fields for easy filtering and joins. Use this as the normalized base when analyzing request volumes, times-to-close, neighborhood or district breakdowns, and joins to spatial/neighborhood data. | Use for: time series of 311 requests (daily/monthly); average/median time-to-close by category or agency; spatial distribution of requests using latitude/longitude or neighborhood; counts by status, category, complaint_type, or supervisor_district

views.name: bikeshare_stations_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  name AS station_name,
  short_name,
  lat AS latitude,
  lon AS longitude,
  region_id,
  rental_methods,
  capacity,
  external_id,
  eightd_has_key_dispenser,
  has_kiosk,
  station_geom
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info`
views.description: Normalized station dimension for bikeshare: cleans station_id, exposes coordinates, capacity, region and kiosk/dispensers flags. Use to join trips, status snapshots, and regions. station_id is kept as STRING to match station_status; casts may be needed when joining to bikeshare_trips which uses INT ids. | Use for: station inventory and capacities; spatial joins to neighborhoods or region-level aggregations; joining to station status snapshots and trips

views.name: bikeshare_station_status_snapshots
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(last_reported) AS reported_ts,
  last_reported AS last_reported_epoch,
  num_bikes_available,
  num_bikes_disabled,
  num_docks_available,
  num_docks_disabled,
  SAFE_CAST(num_ebikes_available AS INT64) AS num_ebikes_available,
  is_installed,
  is_renting,
  is_returning,
  eightd_has_available_keys
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_status`
grain: one row per station status snapshot (station_id + last_reported)
views.description: Aggregated station status snapshots per station report time: exposes measures (bikes/docks available/disabled), booleans (installed/renting/returning), and readable last_reported timestamp. Useful for time-series analysis, capacity checks, and computing availability trends. One row per station_id + last_reported (POSIX epoch) snapshot. | Use for: time series of bikes/docks availability; compute peak/trough availability per station; join latest snapshot per station with station dim

views.name: bikeshare_trips_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  duration_sec,
  start_date AS start_ts,
  end_date AS end_ts,
  start_station_name,
  SAFE_CAST(start_station_id AS INT64) AS start_station_id,
  end_station_name,
  SAFE_CAST(end_station_id AS INT64) AS end_station_id,
  bike_number,
  zip_code,
  subscriber_type,
  c_subscription_type,
  start_station_latitude,
  start_station_longitude,
  end_station_latitude,
  end_station_longitude,
  member_birth_year,
  member_gender
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
views.description: Normalized bikeshare trips table: preserves trip identifiers, timestamps, station ids (kept as INT64 where provided), coordinates, member attributes, and duration. Use as the canonical trips fact for duration, origin/destination, subscriber analyses, and joining to station dimension (may need cast of station_id). | Use for: trip duration distributions by subscriber type or time of day; origin-destination matrices (start_station_id -> end_station_id); join trips to station dimension after casting station ids

views.name: bikeshare_station_latest_status_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  last_reported AS last_reported_epoch,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(last_reported) AS reported_ts,
  num_bikes_available,
  num_docks_available,
  is_installed,
  is_renting,
  is_returning,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY last_reported DESC) AS snapshot_rank
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_status`
grain: one row per station snapshot (station_id + last_reported); ranked per station
views.description: Ranked status snapshots per station ordered by report time. Exposes row_rank so downstream queries can select the latest snapshot per station by filtering row_rank = 1. Useful for getting current availability per station without hard-coding time windows. | Use for: select latest status per station (WHERE snapshot_rank = 1); time-aware joins to trips for availability at trip start times (use ranking to pick closest prior snapshot)

views.name: sfpd_incidents_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,

  descript,
  dayofweek,
  pddistrict,
  resolution,
  address,
  longitude,
  latitude,
  location,
  pdid,
  timestamp AS event_ts,
  CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM timestamp) AS DATE) AS event_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_sfpd_incidents.sfpd_incidents`
views.description: Normalized SFPD incidents: preserves unique_key and key descriptive and spatial columns, exposes event timestamp and date for time-series analyses and spatial joins to neighborhoods. | Use for: counts of incidents by category/pddistrict/day; spatial joins to neighborhoods or mapping by lat/lon; time-to-resolution or trends over time

views.name: neighborhoods_geoms

Use for counts of filmings by neighborhood (text matching) or time-series of filming activity. | Use for: counts of filming locations by year or location text; find films shot in a given neighborhood by text match; aggregate directors/actors with most filmed scenes

views.name: bikeshare_station_with_latest_status
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id,
  s.name AS station_name,
  s.lat AS station_latitude,
  s.lon AS station_longitude,
  s.region_id,
  s.capacity,
  s.has_kiosk,
  ss.reported_ts AS status_reported_ts,
  ss.num_bikes_available,
  ss.num_docks_available,
  ss.is_installed,
  ss.is_renting,
  ss.is_returning
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` AS s
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    station_id,
    TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(last_reported) AS reported_ts,
    num_bikes_available,
    num_docks_available,
    is_installed,
    is_renting,
    is_returning
  FROM (
    SELECT
      station_id,
      last_reported,
      num_bikes_available,
      num_docks_available,
      is_installed,
      is_renting,
      is_returning,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY last_reported DESC) AS rn
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_status`
  )
  WHERE rn = 1
) AS ss
ON s.station_id = ss.station_id
grain: one row per station (station_id) with latest known status
views.description: Join station dimension to its latest status snapshot (use snapshot_rank = 1 on bikeshare_station_latest_status_rank). Exposes station static attributes alongside most-recent availability metrics. Useful for current availability dashboards and joins to trips for origin/destination availability comparisons. | Use for: current availability per station; capacity vs available bikes/docks ratios; map stations colored by availability
